contract.api: limit_paired_wheel_speeds(current array2, desired array2, max_accel, sim_dt) -> {applied array2, alpha}
contract.invalid: nonfinite current/desired/maxa/dt or negative maxa/dt throws invalid_argument
contract.normal: one common alpha from source-current pair; exact binary64 result stays within each rim a*dt budget; inward rounding may make alpha smaller than nominal
contract.reset: stateless helper: caller clears command/epoch; no old instruction accumulator

derivation: zero target: common alpha=min(1,a*dt/M), each rim and body v/w multiply by1-alpha
holding old speed adds at most .30*.034; an additional full phase adds .0102m
assumptions: ideal no-slip differential-drive mapping and instantaneous tracking of applied joint target
source-current joint feedback is accurate; no stale accumulated instruction
initial body abs(v)<=.30 and abs(w)<=1.2 at braking start; rim acceleration limit1
sim-time wheel updates at most34ms; reaction within declared.16s; zero command retained
numeric inward rounding may reduce alpha; negligible binary64 arithmetic must be audited separately
limitations: current joint target step bound is not a world body speed/acceleration guarantee
torque, contact, slip and real tracking are omitted; native full-vector/stop audits remain mandatory
global stop envelope is not a claim of instantaneous minimum body deceleration.5m/s2
grid complements the closed-form upper bound and does not substitute native evidence
